task.title: First start
task.shortdesc: This is a basic workflow with the compressor as your only pedal.

taskbody.prereq: Before you begin, make sure the pedal has power.
taskbody.context: Starting from basic settings, try to experiment with all the knobs to get an effect you enjoy.

step.cmd: Plug in the cable from your guitar into the IN jack input.
Run a different cable from the pedal's OUT jack to your amplifier or audio interface.
You can start off with the following settings on the pedal:

ol.li: RELEASE, ATTACK, OUTPUT, and INPUT knobs at 12 o'clock.

step.cmd: Press the footswitch to turn on the pedal.
Looking at the GAIN REDUCTION meter, rotate the INPUT knob so that you see a range from 3 to 7 lights on the meter while playing your guitar normally:
Rotate the OUTPUT knob to the desired overall volume.
Rotate the ATTACK knob clockwise to soften the initial attack of your note or counterclockwise to accentuate it.
Rotate the RELEASE knob clockwise to make the compression effect last longer or counterclockwise to make it fade faster.

Use the RATIO knob to define the strength of compression. The bigger the setting (up to 20:1), the more volume will be decreased when compression is in effect. For example, the 4:1 setting means that, for every 4 dB over the threshold, only 1 dB comes through.

taskbody.result: Once you have dialed in the desired compression, you can start playing as-is or add other effects after the compressor in your signal chain.
